Project finance & ESIA

Dated land evidence for project finance, ESIA and resettlement

A dated, reviewed record of the structures in a project footprint on the cut-off date, baselines your ESIA and RAP teams can build on, and dated evidence of what changed between site visits. Built to support your census, your monitoring plan and your legal and community processes, never to replace them.

Tell us about your project footprint How the method works

The problem, in your words

The dates that matter most are the hardest to evidence

Resettlement, ESIA and lender monitoring all turn on the same questions: what stood on this land on a given date, what has changed since, and can anyone show it. Site visits answer them on the day of the visit. Dated imagery answers them in between.

“We need a structure count before the field census starts.”

Planning the census, the enumerator teams and the consultation schedule needs a number and a map of the footprint before anyone goes to the field.

“Structures appear after the cut-off date and turn into claims.”

Under IFC Performance Standard 5, the census and a published cut-off date exist to discourage ineligible people, such as opportunistic settlers, from claiming benefits. That only works if you can show what was there on the day.

“We can’t visit as often as the monitoring plan requires.”

Lenders’ monitors and supervision teams visit a few times a year. Clearing, construction and new settlement carry on between visits.

“When did the clearing start?”

An authorisation audit or a rectification application needs to know roughly when ground was cleared or built on, and whether it was inside the approved footprint.

“What’s the land history before financial close?”

Due diligence on a site, a route or an asset being acquired needs a dated view of what was built, cleared or changed, and roughly when.

“What was there on that date?”

A grievance about one plot, one house or one field needs every dated image of that point in one place.

Who this is for

  • Resettlement, RAP and land-acquisition managers on lender-financed projects
  • ESIA, RAP and EAP consultancies: RAP leads, census coordinators, GIS managers
  • DFI and export-credit E&S specialists and supervision teams
  • Independent E&S consultants, lenders’ advisers and third-party monitoring agents
  • Project implementation units and their M&E officers
  • Borrowers’ E&S compliance managers
  • Environmental control officers and environmental lawyers
  • M&A and due-diligence teams
  • Grievance officers

Resettlement cut-off-date records

A dated register for the day the cut-off is set

IFC Performance Standard 5 says the client “is not required to compensate or assist those who encroach on the project area after the cut-off date for eligibility, provided the cut-off date has been clearly established and made public” (PS5, para. 23). The weak point in practice is the evidence: showing, months later, what stood in the footprint on the day.

We produce a dated record of the structures in the project footprint on the imagery dates around your cut-off, with the imagery, coordinates and a stable ID for each structure. Reviewers tag each one with what the imagery shows, such as main building, outbuilding, livestock enclosure or under construction, and in dense villages or under tree cover they mark structures by hand rather than rely on automatic detection. The record is fixed with file fingerprints and an independent timestamp.

After the cut-off, the footprint is re-surveyed on a schedule agreed with you. New structures are flagged between dated surveys and confirmed by a reviewer, so your team can show which arrived after the date. Only dated imagery is used for this work: a drone survey, a dated satellite scene or your own imagery, never an undated basemap.

  1. Before the census

    A structure layer and estimated households to plan fieldwork, enumerator teams and consultation.

  2. At the cut-off date

    A dated register with IDs and categories, and an evidence pack that fixes it.

  3. After the cut-off

    Scheduled re-surveys, with new structures flagged, confirmed and packaged.

  4. When a claim arrives

    A location sheet with every dated image of the plot, compared with the cut-off register.

Supports, never replaces

The register supports your census and asset inventory under IFC Performance Standard 5 and World Bank ESS5. It does not set the cut-off date, determine eligibility or replace the field census, and categories describe what the imagery shows, not who lives in a building or who owns it.

Baselines for ESIA and RAP teams

A supplier to your consultancy, not a competitor

ESIA and RAP consultancies need structure data quickly, in formats their own GIS teams can map, for reports they sign. We work as a supplier to those teams. We deliver structure layers across the study area, reviewer categories, reviewer-led mapping for dense villages, settlement growth trends and estimated households with the assumptions stated, all as layers your consultants put in their own maps.

For alternatives analysis, we count the structures each route or site option would affect and screen each for slope, drainage crossings and flood exposure. A land-use and land-cover baseline adds built-up land, cropland, bare ground, water and tree cover around the project. If your team has already flown the site, we run the same analysis on your drone imagery.

Reports and layers come in English or Portuguese, and the work sits inside your deliverable: we are not named on your report unless you want us to be.

What you receive

  • Structure layers across the study area, with categories
  • Reviewer-led mapping for dense villages
  • Estimated households, with an assumptions table
  • Settlement growth trends
  • A land-use and land-cover baseline
  • A comparison table of route or site options
  • Terrain and flood-exposure screening
  • GIS layers for your consultants’ own maps

Dated evidence between site visits

What changed on the ground since the last mission

The Equator Principles ask for independent monitoring and reporting after financial close (EP4, Principle 9), and DFI supervision missions visit on a cycle. Between visits, dated imagery shows the construction footprint and earthworks compared between dates, new structures in footprints and buffers, clearing outside the approved areas and revegetation where it was promised. Drone orthophotos of resettlement villages show construction progress, subject to the permits and authorisations each job requires.

After a flood or cyclone, a reviewer’s before-and-after check shows visible damage to structures and assets. Dated archive scenes and new captures fill the gaps between drone visits, and imagery the project already holds can be analysed the same way.

Remote evidence complements site visits. It helps the monitor decide where to go and what to ask, and it never replaces the visit itself.

What you receive

  • Construction footprint and earthworks compared between dates
  • New structures in footprints and buffers, reviewer-confirmed
  • Clearing outside approved areas, and revegetation
  • Progress at resettlement villages from drone orthophotos, subject to permits
  • Before-and-after checks after floods and cyclones
  • Dated archive scenes, new captures or your own imagery
  • Evidence packs for each monitoring period

Grievances and claims

Every dated image of one plot, in one place

When a grievance names a single plot, house or field, a location sheet gathers every dated image that covers it, so your grievance officer can see what was there on each date. The imagery history of the parcel shows roughly when things were built or cleared, the sheet can be compared with the cut-off register, and an evidence pack fixes what was shared. It supports an investigation; it never decides the claim.

Evidence packs & grievance checks

Dated imagery, registers and maps packaged with file fingerprints and an independent timestamp, to support legal and community processes.

Environmental authorisation compliance

Roughly when clearing or construction happened

Environmental control officers, developers’ environmental managers and environmental lawyers often need to know roughly when ground was cleared or built on, and whether it was inside the authorised footprint. Archived imagery shows what changed and roughly when; clearing and construction footprints compared between dates show where; and structures and activity inside the no-go buffers you define are listed.

A land-cover baseline before development, and revegetation tracked on rehabilitated areas afterwards, give the before-and-after picture. The evidence supports audits and applications; it does not prove compliance or non-compliance.

What you receive

  • An imagery history showing roughly when clearing or construction happened
  • Clearing and construction footprints compared between dates
  • Structures and activity inside the no-go buffers you define
  • A pre-development land-cover baseline, and revegetation tracking
  • An evidence pack for the audit or application

Land due diligence

Before financial close, investment or acquisition

Before a lender commits, or a buyer takes on a site, a route or a concession, a dated view of the land shows what has been built, cleared or changed and roughly when. We combine the imagery history, a land-cover baseline and dated scenes with the current structures on the rights of way, inside the concessions and in the hazard zones of the assets involved, and fix the baseline at completion with an evidence pack.

How much archive exists varies by place, and this is not a title, tenure or valuation check, or a quantification of liabilities.

The full list of services behind this page

Encroachment and structure mapping

  • Right-of-way encroachment surveyA register of the structures within the distances you choose from your pipeline, power line, road or railway. Each structure comes with its distance to the line and its coordinates, and each stretch of the route gets an encroachment-density rating.
  • Concession, site and boundary encroachment surveyStructures inside your concession, site or land-use boundary, in a ring around it, or both, mapped and listed so you can see where land is being occupied.
  • Structures in hazard and impact zonesStructures inside the zones you define, such as tailings dam-break inundation areas, blast and exclusion zones, flood lines or safety setbacks, each listed with its location and distance to the source.
  • Route and site option comparisonSide-by-side structure counts along alternative pipeline, line or road alignments, or across candidate sites, so land impact can be weighed before a route is fixed.
  • Area-wide structure mappingA GIS layer of structures across a whole district, concession or imagery survey, ready to load into your own mapping system.
  • Reviewer-led structure mappingWhere automatic detection is not enough, such as dense villages, mixed tree cover or unusual roofs, AfriScan reviewers mark structures by hand on high-resolution imagery.
  • Structure categories and attributesA reviewer tags each structure with what the imagery shows, such as main building, outbuilding, livestock enclosure, under construction or roof type, for resettlement and planning registers.

Change and repeat surveys

  • Change detection between dated surveysNew and removed structures between two or more dated surveys, flagged automatically and confirmed by a reviewer, with before-and-after views of each change.
  • Scheduled re-surveys with change noticesYour route or site re-surveyed on a schedule agreed with you, with an email to your team after each survey saying what has changed and where.
  • Settlement growth trendsHow built-up land has changed year by year around your assets, showing where settlement pressure is growing.
  • Vegetation and land-cover changeMaps of where vegetation has been cleared, has regrown or has changed along servitudes, around plantations and forest estates, and across concessions, compared between dates.
  • Rehabilitation and revegetation trackingProgress of revegetation on rehabilitated mine land, closed borrow pits and restored servitudes, tracked between dates.
  • Construction and earthworks progressDated drone orthophotos and elevation models compared side by side, with maps of where ground has been cut or filled between visits.

Terrain, water and hazard screening

  • Flood-exposure screeningStructures, route segments and sites in historically flooded, low-lying or river-crossing areas, highlighted for planning and emergency preparedness.
  • Post-event flood and damage mappingAfter a cyclone or flood, a map of the flooded area and a reviewer's before-and-after check of structures and assets along your route or site.

Mozambique, South Africa, Nigeria

The rules your baseline has to serve

A summary of public rules for orientation, as of 26 September 2026, not legal advice; the sources are linked. Lender standards (IFC Performance Standards, World Bank ESS5, the Equator Principles) apply on top of national law wherever a project is financed by them.

Português · English

Mozambique

Resettlement for economic activities follows Decreto n.º 31/2012, de 8 de Agosto: data collection includes delimiting the area and the current occupation, at least four public consultations are required (art. 23), the district government approves the plan, and a technical commission oversees the process. Environmental impact assessment follows Decreto n.º 54/2015, and in petroleum, Lei n.º 8/2026 art. 61 requires resettled people to receive “condições de vida condignas e superiores”. Reports can be delivered in Portuguese for district government and the resettlement commission, and in insecure areas we never publish settlement maps without the client’s written permission.

English

South Africa

Environmental authorisation runs under NEMA and the EIA Regulations 2014, as amended, with registered environmental assessment practitioners (EAPASA) as the natural channel for baseline work. Lines inside the strategic transmission corridors that meet the DFFE power-line standard (GN 2313) are excluded from environmental authorisation, which moves land baselines earlier, and DFIs and Equator banks finance transmission and independent power projects under IFC PS5. If a register is to be used as evidence about unlawful conduct, POPIA’s prior-authorisation rule (s57) may apply to your organisation: take advice first.

English

Nigeria

World Bank-financed programmes in energy access, transmission and climate resilience apply ESS5. The EIA Act lists the projects that need a mandatory study, including agricultural programmes that resettle a hundred families or more. Under the Land Use Act, resettlement may be offered instead of compensation for a residential building (s.33). The Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 can apply to imagery that shows identifiable homes, so data handling is set out in the proposal.

How it works

From footprint to dated record

  1. Scope

    You send the footprint, the census timetable and what the record is for. We agree the dates, the imagery plan and the deliverables in a written proposal.

  2. Secure dated imagery

    A drone survey, a dated satellite scene, a new capture or your own imagery: never an undated basemap for a record that must reflect a date.

  3. Map and review

    Structures are mapped and a person checks every automatic result, tags categories and marks by hand where automatic detection falls short.

  4. Deliver and fix

    You receive the register, layers and report, and an evidence pack fixes the record with fingerprints and a timestamp.

More detail on how it works, the methodology and how we work, including subcontracts and supplier forms.

Honest scope

What we do, and what we don’t

What we do

  • Record the structures in a footprint on dated imagery, with IDs and categories
  • Flag structures that appear after a date that matters, confirmed by a reviewer
  • Package records with file fingerprints and an independent timestamp
  • Supply layers, estimates and baselines inside your consultants’ deliverables

What we don’t do

  • Set the cut-off date, determine eligibility or value assets
  • Count, identify or interview people, or replace the field census
  • Verify title or tenure, or certify compliance with any standard
  • Replace site visits, independent monitoring or your consultants’ judgement

Frequently asked questions

Is your baseline a substitute for the census and asset inventory?

No. It is a dated record of the structures in the footprint, with imagery, coordinates and IDs, that supports your census and asset inventory under IFC Performance Standard 5. Your field teams still carry out the census and the asset inventory, and categories describe what the imagery shows; compensation needs verification on the ground.

Does the imagery set the cut-off date?

No. The cut-off date comes from your resettlement process, through the host government’s procedure or, where there is none, set by the project and made public. Our dated record documents what was on the ground on the imagery dates around it.

How do you show structures that appeared after the cut-off date?

We re-survey the footprint on a schedule agreed with you, flag new structures between dated surveys, have a reviewer confirm them, and package the results with file fingerprints and an independent timestamp.

Can the evidence be used in a dispute or in court?

Our evidence packs support legal and community processes; how they are used is for you and your lawyers to decide, and we make no claim about how a court will treat them. The fingerprints and timestamp show that the files existed at that time and haven’t changed since; they don’t prove how the imagery was captured.

Can you work as a subcontractor to our ESIA or RAP team?

Yes. We supply structure baselines, estimated households, land-use baselines and GIS layers for your own maps and reports, in English or Portuguese, under your project’s confidentiality terms.

Can you get imagery for a specific date?

Archive coverage and dates vary by place. Where archive imagery is too old we can request a new satellite capture, but its date depends on satellite availability and weather and is never guaranteed. For a date that matters, we plan the imagery in the proposal.

Does remote evidence replace site visits?

No. It gives you dated evidence between visits and helps you plan where visits are needed. It is not independent verification and does not replace the monitoring your lenders or regulators require.

How are household numbers produced?

As estimates, from structure counts and stated persons-per-household assumptions drawn from national census data. Every report sets out the assumptions, and reviewer categories that separate main buildings from outbuildings make the estimate better.

Send the footprint or corridor, the census timetable and what the record is for. We reply with a scope, an imagery plan and a written proposal, as a supplier to you or to your consultants.
